title: 第262章 审判之焰空名骑士第266章 审判之焰血拓
slug: 黯潮纪元异世界的崛起
lines: 盔甲的护喉里吐出最后一个音节时，声音断了。
不是停。是像录音带被剪刀截断，那个音节的尾音还在空气里震，但后面的部分——编号的最后一段——被火焰吞掉了。陈默跪在五米外，膝盖骨压在地砖裂缝上，空剑横在膝前。他看到盔甲胸甲的火焰纹路在编号末尾处烧出一个缺口，像有人用橡皮擦掉了一行字。
“契约编号——”盔甲重复，声音比刚才低了一个音阶。
又断了。
同一位置。火焰纹路在胸甲上跳了一下，缺口的边缘烧成焦黑色，像被烙铁烫过的伤口。陈默盯着那个缺口，脊椎里窜过一阵冷。不是恐惧。是考古学家的直觉——他在三星堆见过类似的东西：青铜器上被故意磨掉的铭文，被凿子敲掉的名字。统治者死后，继任者会把前任的名字从祭祀器上刮掉，让他的灵魂在另一个世界也找不到归宿。
盔甲低下头，面罩的竖缝对准胸甲上的缺口。
“第二见证无法读取完整的契约编号。”它的声音没有起伏，火焰在护喉里翻滚，“契约最后一段被烧断。不是自然磨损，是外力抹除。”
陈默的喉咙发干。空剑的剑刃贴着他的膝盖，冰凉的，不像是火焰编出来的东西。他试着开口，声带震了一下，发出一个沙哑的气音：“第二见证——”
“不是审判者。”盔甲打断他，面罩的竖缝从胸甲转向陈默的脸，“我不审判你的罪行。我只确认一件事：你，跪在裂缝地砖上的人，是否还是雷诺·艾德伍德。”
陈默的嘴唇动了动。
不是。他想说。我不是雷诺。我是陈默，三星堆考古队的，地震那天掉进坑里，醒来就在这个身体里。但话卡在喉咙里没出来。因为他看到盔甲胸甲的火焰纹路在他沉默的瞬间亮了一度，像某种感应器在等待一个特定的波长。
“圣殿骑士誓词。”盔甲说，“念出来。契约会验证你的声音。”
陈默握紧空剑的剑柄。手指嵌进火焰纹路的凹槽里，指尖传来一阵刺麻，像被静电打过。他想到第260章时，火焰从门缝里涌出来，在他身上烧出契约烙印——那些烙印不是普通的骑士印记，是能读取灵魂语言的旧日契约接口。
念誓词等于承认自己是雷诺。
不念呢？
“你不念，不代表你拒绝。”盔甲的面罩竖缝里透出一丝白光，像瞳孔在暗处收缩，“沉默本身也是一种回应。契约会把它解读为——雷诺·艾德伍德已无法确认自己的身份。”
火焰开始往上升。
不是攻击。是审判厅的四面墙壁同时亮起火焰纹路，从地砖的裂缝里钻出来，沿着墙壁往上爬，在穹顶汇成一个圆环。陈默看到圆环的内圈刻着文字——不是埃尔德兰通用语，是一种更古老的符号，每个字符都在缓慢旋转，像齿轮咬合。
誓词圆环。
他的心脏在胸腔里猛撞了一下。肋骨被压紧，肺里的空气被挤出去。不是恐惧。是身体在替雷诺做反应——雷诺的肌肉记住了这个圆环，记住了念完誓词后会发生什么。
“你不念，我来念。”盔甲说。
它的护喉里开始吐出音节。不是埃尔德兰语，是圣殿骑士的契约语言，每个音节都像金属片被掰断。陈默的牙关咬紧，下颌骨的关节发出咯吱声——不是他要咬，是雷诺的咬肌在自动收缩，像身体在抵抗某种召唤。
第一个音节落进圆环时，陈默的左肩抖了一下。
肩胛骨往内收，锁骨往下压，整条左臂像被人从肩膀处往下拽。空剑在膝前震了一下，剑刃碰到地砖，发出一声脆响。
第二个音节。
右肩。
第三个音节。
颈椎。
陈默听到自己的脊柱一节接一节地发出咔嗒声，像有人在拧螺丝。他的头开始往下低——不是他自己要低头，是颈椎被一个看不见的力往下压，下巴朝胸口靠近。
誓词在把他压回献祭姿势。
“够了。”陈默从牙缝里挤出两个字。
盔甲停住了。不是被他的话打断，是它在等他说话。面罩的竖缝对准他的脸，火焰在护喉里安静下来，像一只竖起耳朵的猫。

##一
The voice broke as the last syllable came out of the armor's gorget.
Not stop. It was like a tape being cut by scissors. The end of that syllable was still vibrating in the air, but the following part - the last section of the number - was swallowed up by the flames. Chen Mo knelt five meters away, his kneecaps pressing against the cracks in the floor tiles, and the empty sword lying across his knees. He saw that the flame pattern on the armor's breastplate had burned a gap at the end of the number, as if someone had erased a line of writing with an eraser.
"Contract number——" the armor repeated, his voice lower than before.
It broke again.
same location. Flame patterns danced on the breastplate, and the edge of the gap burned black, like a wound burned by a soldering iron. Chen Mo stared at the gap, and a chill ran down his spine. Not fear. It was the archaeologist's intuition - he had seen similar things in Sanxingdui: inscriptions on bronze vessels that were deliberately worn away, and names that were knocked out by chisels. After a ruler dies, his successor will scratch off the predecessor's name from the sacrificial vessel so that his soul cannot find a home in another world.
The armor lowered its head, aligning the vertical seams of the mask with the gaps in the breastplate.
"The second witness cannot read the complete contract number." Its voice did not rise and fall, and the flames rolled in the gorget. "The last section of the contract was burned off. It was not natural wear and tear, but erasure by external forces."
Chen Mo's throat was dry. The blade of the empty sword was close to his knees. It was cold and did not look like something made of flames. He tried to speak, but his vocal cords vibrated and he made a hoarse breath: "The second witness——"
"Not a judge." The armor interrupted him, and the vertical slits of the mask turned from the breastplate to Chen Mo's face, "I will not judge your crimes. I only confirm one thing: whether you, the person kneeling on the cracked floor tiles, are still Reno Edwood."
Chen Mo's lips moved.
no. He wanted to say. I'm not Reno. I am Chen Mo, from the Sanxingdui archaeological team. I fell into a pit on the day of the earthquake and woke up in this body. But the words got stuck in his throat and didn't come out. Because he saw the flame pattern on the armor's breastplate brighten a degree during his silent moment, like some kind of sensor waiting for a specific wavelength.
"The Templar Oath," the armor said, "say it. The contract will validate your voice."
Chen Mo clenched the hilt of the empty sword. His fingers were embedded in the grooves of the flame pattern, and there was a tingling sensation on his fingertips, as if he had been hit by static electricity. When he thought about Chapter 260, flames poured out from the crack in the door, burning contract marks on his body - those marks were not ordinary knight marks, they were old contract interfaces that could read the language of the soul.
Reciting the oath is equivalent to admitting that one is Renault.
Don’t you want to read it?
"Just because you don't read it doesn't mean you refuse." A ray of white light came out from the vertical slit of the armor's mask, like pupils shrinking in the dark. "Silence itself is also a response. The contract will interpret it as - Reno Edwood can no longer confirm his identity."
The flames began to rise.
Not an attack. It was the four walls of the trial hall that lit up with flame patterns at the same time, emerging from the cracks in the floor tiles, climbing up the walls, and forming a ring on the dome. Chen Mo saw words engraved on the inner circle of the ring - not the common language of Eldran, but an older symbol. Each character was slowly rotating, like gears meshing.
Oath circle.
His heart hammered in his chest. His ribs were compressed and the air was squeezed out of his lungs. Not fear. It was the body that was reacting for Renault - Renault's muscles remembered the ring and what would happen after reciting the oath.
"If you don't want to read it, I will." Armor said.
Syllables began to flow from its gorget. Not Eldran, but the indentured language of the Templars, each syllable broken like a piece of metal. Chen Mo clenched his teeth, and the joints of his mandible made a creaking sound - it was not that he wanted to bite, but that Renault's masseter muscles were contracting automatically, as if his body was resisting some kind of call.
When the first syllable fell into the ring, Chen Mo's left shoulder shook.
The shoulder blades are drawn inwards, the clavicle is pressed down, and the entire left arm seems to be pulled down from the shoulder. The empty sword shook in front of his knees, and the blade made a crisp sound when it hit the floor tiles.
second syllable.
Right shoulder.
The third syllable.
Cervical vertebrae.
Chen Mo heard his spine clicking one after another, like someone was tightening screws. His head began to lower - it wasn't because he was lowering his head, but because his cervical vertebrae were being pressed down by an invisible force, and his chin moved closer to his chest.
The oath was forcing him back to the sacrificial position.
"That's enough." Chen Mo squeezed out two words through his teeth.
The armor stopped. It wasn't interrupted by his words, it was waiting for him to speak. The vertical slit of the mask was pointed at his face, and the flames quieted down in the gorget, like a cat with its ears pricked up.
